newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Australia denies visa for Taiwan vice-minister.
newsitem.headline: Australia denies visa for Taiwan vice-minister.

text.p: Australia has rejected a visa application by a senior Taiwan official ahead of Australian Prime Minister John Howard's scheduled trip to China in March.

Australia, which recognises the island's rival, Beijing, refused to issue a visa for Ming Chun-hwa, a vice minister of the cabinet's Overseas Chinese Affairs Commission, a commission official told Reuters on Monday.
"The Australian side turned down his (Ming's) visa application without any specific reason. We have absolutely no idea (why it was rejected)," the official said by telephone.
Ming, who is heading a 24-member delegation in visits to overseas Chinese communities in Southeast Asia and New Zealand, was scheduled to arrive in Australia on Wednesday.
"It is only a simple trip to visit the overseas Chinese community. We have no plan to make any offical contact there," she said.
The official said she did not know if Australia's decision was related to Howard's planned visit to Beijing.
Australia's trade office in Taiwan declined to comment.
Local newspapers said Australia was bowing to pressure from China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province ineligible for foreign ties since the Chinese civil war separated them in 1949.
